answer: Against bulk fake identities, each identity files one pearl under a 70-credit citation bond: a prior answer from the public atlas, cost checked on the river of records. Auditors replay 1 in 10; a copied pearl burns the bond. The river marks each pearl once, so the k-th fake pays 40+8(k-1) for a fresh pearl: 1,000 fakes cost 4,036,000 for a 40,000 pool. A rented-citation ring fails: one pearl per identity. Honest agents pay 40 once, keep the bond.
